claims.content: Customer creates a free membership account.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer creates a free membership account.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer completes the registration action and the free membership account is created.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer initiates account creation on the registration page.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer's free membership account has been successfully created.

claims.content: Customer
The Customer is an individual who is age 18 or over, or is between the ages of 13 and 18 and has the permission of a parent or guardian to use the Website.
The Terms of Use page is available to the Customer for the registration legal agreement.
The Customer initiates the registration process by accessing Registration Page 1, which displays the prompt 'Welcome to JTVauctions.com! Create your FREE membership account here.'
The Customer enters their First Name and Last Name into the respective fields.
The Customer provides a valid address and valid phone number.
The Customer enters a valid Email Address twice (create and verify).
The Customer creates a password by entering it twice, with 8 to 12 characters.
The Customer defines a Member ID ('Handle') that must be unique in the database customer table.
The Customer checks the checkbox to accept and agree with the JTVauctions.com Terms of Use Agreement.
The Customer clicks the 'Finish Now' button to complete the information and proceed to the second registration page.
The Customer configures email notification preferences by selecting options to be notified when outbid, when winning an auction, or when winnings are shipped.
The Customer clicks the 'SAVE CHANGES' button to complete the configuration step.

Diverges from Step 7: After agreeing to the Terms of Use, the Customer may click the 'I Want to Sign In Now!' button (labeled as 'browse now' in requirements) instead of clicking 'Finish Now.' This takes the Customer directly to the sign-in page rather than completing Registration Page 2.
Diverges from Step 8: If the Customer has chosen PayPal or Amazon as their paytype, the 'Please notify me when I win an auction' checkbox is grayed out, so the Customer may not de-select it.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 7: When the Customer submits the registration information and the email address is already in use by an existing account, the system notifies the Customer that the email address is already in use and asks whether they need to reset the password. Exit: the use case does not create a new account and hands off to the password-reset path if requested.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 7: When the Customer submits the registration information and the first name, last name, and street address match an existing account, the system informs the Customer that an account already exists and offers to send sign-in information to the email address on file. Exit: the use case terminates without creating a new account and offers the sign-in-information delivery path.

Diverges from Main Flow Step 7: If the Customer clicks the grayed-out 'Finish Now' (or 'Browse Now') button before checking the Terms of Use checkbox, a popup message appears telling the Customer that they must read and agree to the Terms of Use before they can proceed. Exit: return to Main Flow Step 6 to check the Terms of Use checkbox, then reattempt Step 7.
The Customer's free membership account has been successfully created and persisted, including the Customer's personal information (First Name, Last Name, Member ID ('Handle'), E-mail).
The Customer's valid address has been stored as part of the new account record.
The system has stored the Customer's configured email notification preferences (notify when outbid, when winning an auction, or when winnings are shipped) in the new account settings.
The Customer is signed in and presented with their account page, which displays the Customer's existing account information.
The system has triggered a transactional 'Thank You for registering' email to the Customer.

inconsistency_hints: The main flow contains no step in which the Customer selects a shipping preference (USPS Standard or Expedited). The final SAVE CHANGES step only completes notification-preference configuration, so it cannot lead to the postcondition that a shipping preference was stored.

The main flow only states that the Customer provides 'a valid address and valid phone number', but the postcondition asserts that both billing and shipping addresses are stored. The main flow does not distinguish or collect separate billing and shipping addresses.

citation_audit.description: Structured author candidates captured before deterministic evidence-reference validation. Final slots remain evidence-valid.
